hypothesis: A validation-only repair admits ordinary-vectorized affine scalar-fission producers whose generated completed-count increment loses nuw, using the existing one-way integer refinement rule. It should unblock the retained descending and four modular early-exit controls while preserving exact actual-count provenance. LLVM compiler transformations, admission, profitability, the C execution harness and the immutable 117 primary inputs are unchanged.
semantics: Only the generated %fission.completed definition gains the existing affine_instruction_refines relation against add nuw i64 %fission.ordinal, 1. The result SSA identity, add opcode, i64 width, ordered ordinal/1 operands and latch block must match. Candidate flags may only be a subset of the emitted nuw contract, so nuw or no flags are accepted; nsw, nuw nsw, exact, disjoint and duplicate flags are not newly permitted. Dropping nuw replaces poison on overflow with a wrapping integer value and leaves every originally defined execution unchanged. More strongly, the compiler admission proves a finite producer DAG with one latch visit per entered iteration, including the exiting iteration, and a representable N<=M. Here M=65 and CountTy=i64: before iteration i the ordinal is i, its unique latch add produces i+1, and final completed=N cannot overflow. A modular original induction can exit before its equality storage witness: the ordinal still counts actual completed iterations, not n. Zero entry does not enter producer or consumer. The ordinal PHI remains exactly [0,preheader] (inner.ph for enclosing reuse), [completed,latch]; the completed export remains exactly phi i64 [completed,latch] in consumer.ph. Unique definitions, exact block placement and all original instruction/control/metadata preservation checks remain. The existing small guard/control/SSA certificates alone may justify n or observed expanded N=n expressions; no certificate or bound substitution is added. Early-exit siblings still require completed or its verified export, and compaction still requires actual P, the P=0 bypass and unchanged initial states. The owning lit RUN directly calls the production checker on both increment spellings, metadata, analogous controls and specialized boundary arguments; the retained IR is only a checker fixture, never compiled as an executable reference. Fresh executable verification must transform the original scalar IR with real opt after one and two ordinary LV invocations, compare to both original IR and independent C references, and retain exact producer/latch/participant/vector/tail visits, zero entry, empty streams, aliases, canaries, inactive invalid operands, ordered FP bits/signed zero and enclosing-row reuse. Strict and explicitly enabled fission FP reordering remain separate; no FP or errno relaxation is added.
costs: Validation-only: no target allocation, scratch traffic, input reread, recomputation, producer duplication, runtime guard, compiler analysis or profitability change. One existing scalar-integer refinement comparison is added per ordinal fixture function; it is constant size. Existing normalized instruction sets/SSA maps, bounded control/expansion templates and small CFG scans remain; no solver, enumeration or new general analysis machinery is introduced. Regression mutations are finite and operate on printed fixtures only. Underlying scratch costs are unchanged: capacity M times unique contribution allocation sizes plus padding, entry allocated and capped by the existing 65536-byte per-candidate limit and signed pointer-index ceiling. Mixed M=65 cases account for 1044 bytes (65*i32+65*double+65*float, including 4 padding bytes), with 16*N logical store bytes and 16*N load bytes, or 16*P each for compaction. Enclosing rows reuse 784 accounted bytes (65*i32+65*double plus padding), with 12*N stores and 12*N loads per row, without multiplying capacity by rows. Scalar capacity fixtures reserve 4/1020/65536 bytes for 1/255/16384 i32 contributions and transfer 8*N bytes total (131072 at the ceiling). Noncanonical producers have one ordinal PHI, one unit latch add (emitted nuw, possibly unflagged after ordinary LV), and one completed export; compact producers count participants and keep the existing empty guard. No mask arrays, contribution recomputation, original-input rereads, alias/SCEV versioning guards, dynamic or unbounded storage are introduced. Physical stack traffic, register pressure, RVV execution and speedup remain unmeasured.
limitations: The worker ran no build, compiler (including host compilation), lit RUN, VectorizeTests, execution checker, test runner or try.sh. Only source/immutable artifact/JSON inspection and editing were performed. Fresh validation is pending. No compiler-path or new semantic transformation is introduced here. Unseen LV2 or scalar-tail output can still expose another narrowly diagnosable validation failure; no new arithmetic/count form is preemptively accepted. Existing bounded certificates still reject arbitrary equivalent guards, expansions or hoisting. Inherited compiler limitations include non-affine/pointer/FP controls, arbitrary non-strict/non-lattice exits, unbounded/unrepresentable counts, oversized untiled per-candidate scratch, producer cycles/extra recurrences, unsupported effects/live-outs/calls, independent participation streams and strictfp/constrained FP. Host fixed-vscale scalar-remainder execution is not EVL/VP host execution or RVV target execution; RVV machine verification is code generation, not a speedup measurement. No newly selected primary benchmark, direction maturity or performance improvement is claimed. Benchmarks, the harness, other worktrees, binaries, Git index/history/refs and unfinished d2 work were not modified.
